lesson.explanation: Goods are things you can buy and hold. Services are jobs people do for you, like a haircut or a dental cleaning.
lesson.example: A teeth cleaning is a service; a toothbrush is a good.

Do the small activity.

skills.subject: Social Studies

skills.title: Add a two-digit and one-digit number
skills.summary: Add ones to ones; make a new ten if needed.

lesson.explanation: Add the ones first. If they make 10 or more, that makes a new ten.
tutorSteps: Build with tens and ones.
Combine ones; trade 10 ones for a ten.
Record the answer.

skills.reinforcement: Leads to two-digit plus two-digit addition.
skills.subject: Math

skills.title: Spell CVC words
skills.summary: Spell short-vowel words by sound.

lesson.explanation: Stretch the word slowly and write a letter for each sound.
tutorSteps: Model it on paper while talking through it.
Child tries it.
Check with the checklist and fix one thing.

items.prompt: Tutor says: dog, sun, pig, bed, cat. Child writes them.
Tutor says: fish, chop, duck. Child writes them.

skills.reinforcement: Spelling grows with each phonics lesson.
skills.subject: Writing

skills.title: Compound words
skills.summary: Read words made of two smaller words.

lesson.explanation: A compound word joins two words: sun + set = sunset.
tutorSteps: Say the sound or pattern and show it in a word.
Child reads each word aloud; tutor marks it.
Use each word in a sentence.

skills.subject: Reading

skills.title: Add tens to a two-digit number
skills.summary: Add a multiple of 10 to any two-digit number.

lesson.explanation: Only the tens change: 34 + 20 → 3 tens + 2 tens = 5 tens, keep 4 ones → 54.
tutorSteps: Use a 120 chart: move down rows.
Use tens rods.
Practice.

skills.reinforcement: Mental math strategy for all larger numbers.
skills.subject: Math

skills.title: Syllables
skills.summary: Clap and read two-syllable words.

lesson.explanation: A syllable is a beat with one vowel sound. Split long words into beats: rab-bit, nap-kin.
tutorSteps: Say the sound or pattern and show it in a word.
Child reads each word aloud; tutor marks it.
Use each word in a sentence.

skills.subject: Reading

skills.title: Subtract tens from two-digit numbers
skills.summary: Take away multiples of 10.

lesson.explanation: Only the tens change: 75 − 30 → 7 tens − 3 tens = 4 tens, keep 5 ones → 45.
tutorSteps: Use a 120 chart: move up rows.
Use tens rods.
Practice.

skills.reinforcement: Leads to two-digit subtraction with regrouping.
skills.subject: Math

skills.title: Contractions
skills.summary: Read words like can't, I'm, it's.

lesson.explanation: A contraction squeezes two words together; an apostrophe replaces the missing letters.
tutorSteps: Say the sound or pattern and show it in a word.
Child reads each word aloud; tutor marks it.
Use each word in a sentence.

skills.subject: Reading

skills.title: Write about a picture
skills.summary: Write two sentences about a picture.

lesson.explanation: Look carefully. Tell who, what is happening, and one detail.
lesson.example: The girl flies a kite. The kite is red.
tutorSteps: Model it on paper while talking through it.
Child tries it.
Check with the checklist and fix one thing.

items.prompt: Look at any picture book page. Write two sentences about it.

skills.subject: Writing

skills.title: Round to the nearest ten (challenge)
skills.summary: Round two-digit numbers to the nearest 10.

lesson.explanation: Look at the ones: 0–4 round down, 5–9 round up.
tutorSteps: Show the number on a number line between two tens.
Which ten is closer?
Practice.

skills.reinforcement: Estimating answers in every later grade.
skills.subject: Math

skills.title: Weather and seasons
skills.summary: Name the four seasons and weather.

lesson.explanation: The four seasons are spring, summer, fall (autumn) and winter. Each has typical weather.
tutorSteps: Talk about it with a real object or picture.
Do the small activity.
Ask the check questions.

skills.title: American symbols
skills.summary: Know the flag, bald eagle, Statue of Liberty and Liberty Bell.

lesson.explanation: Symbols stand for ideas. The U.S. flag has 50 stars (one for each state) and 13 stripes.
lesson.example: The bald eagle is the national bird.
tutorSteps: Talk about it using the child's own life.
Do the small activity.
Ask the check questions.

items.prompt: How many stars are on the U.S. flag?
How many stripes are on the U.S. flag?

skills.title: Rhyming words

lesson.explanation: Rhyming words end with the same sound: cat, hat, bat.

skills.title: Measure length
skills.summary: Measure with same-size units laid end to end.

lesson.explanation: Line up units with no gaps or overlaps. Count how many units long.
lesson.example: The pencil is 6 paper clips long.
tutorSteps: Measure objects with paper clips or cubes.
Show gaps make wrong answers.
Record lengths.

items.prompt: If a crayon is 4 cubes long and a marker is 6 cubes long, how many cubes longer is the marker?
A book is 10 paper clips long. A notebook is 7. Which is longer?
Measure your table in hand spans. Tutor checks.

skills.summary: Put three objects in order from shortest to longest.

lesson.explanation: Compare two at a time. If A is longer than B and B is longer than C, A is longer than C.

Line them up at one end.

skills.reinforcement: Ordering returns with numbers, fractions and data.

skills.title: Tell time to the hour and half hour
skills.summary: Read an analog clock.

lesson.explanation: The short hand shows the hour. When the long hand points to 12 it is o'clock; to 6 it is half past.
lesson.example: Short hand on 4, long hand on 12 → 4:00
tutorSteps: Use a toy clock.
Move the hands together.
Read times through the day.

skills.reinforcement: Quarter hours and minutes in second grade.

lesson.explanation: We need light to see. When an object blocks light, it makes a shadow.
lesson.example: Your shadow is long in the evening.

Do the small activity.

lesson.explanation: Fluent reading sounds like talking: smooth, not too fast, with feeling at ! and ?

lesson.explanation: Halves: 2 equal parts. Fourths (quarters): 4 equal parts. More parts means smaller parts.
lesson.example: A pizza cut into 4 equal slices shows fourths.
tutorSteps: Fold paper into halves and fourths.
Cut a sandwich into equal parts.

lesson.explanation: Characters are the people or animals in a story. The setting is where and when it happens.

lesson.explanation: Tell what happened first, next and last. Use words like first, then, finally.

Child tries it.

Do the small activity.

lesson.explanation: The main idea is the big point. Details tell more about it.
